leave_behind.item: PR #83 (hauska-mcp-server, this fix) is open, CI-green on all 5 check-runs, deliberately NOT merged and NOT deployed, per this dispatch's own 'Do not' list. Someone with deploy authority needs to merge it, redeploy hauska-mcp-server (confirming first, since this portfolio does not auto-deploy on merge, per the dispatch's own verified note), and then re-run the live falsifiers (export_instrument kind=dossier on 48021:34049 and on a genuinely-resolved parcel) against the ACTUAL deployed surface -- the true customer-facing verification this lane could not itself perform.

This fix necessarily changes a billing-adjacent behavior: before, a hollow refusal never reached authorizePaidCall (zero meters consumed, since the engine was never called); after, a genuinely-hollow parcel now consumes one paid SDK meter for a refused/empty result, because the engine must actually run to know it is hollow. This lane did not reorder metering to avoid it -- that was judged outside this row's scope (a gate-timing fix, not a billing-policy change) and there is an existing regression test pinning authorizePaidCall to exactly one call in this handler that a reorder would have had to touch deliberately, not incidentally. The operator should rule on whether this is acceptable, or whether a follow-on row should refund/skip metering specifically for a hollow result.

fleetMemoryScratch.text: 2026-09-15T19:3x live: hauska-mcp-server serving revision hauska-mcp-server-00092-pur at 100% traffic, image tag rev-3b5626bddf00 (project hauska-prod-497015, region us-central1), confirmed via gcloud run services describe read as JSON. This is the pre-fix state; it will remain the pre-fix state until PR #83 is merged and redeployed.

A 'hollow-report refusal' gate can be technically fail-closed and still be checking the wrong thing entirely: refuseHollowXrayRefresh never had a logic bug, it had an INPUT bug -- it faithfully refused on absent caller-supplied verdict/brief long after those fields stopped being how the system determines hollowness (P-221 moved that determination server-side into the engine). The fix was not 'make the check more lenient', it was 'point the same check at the right data', which is why the message upstreamStatus:'unmeasured' in the original evidence was the correct diagnostic clue the whole time -- it named exactly which side of the call the refusal was firing on.

Before assuming forwarding a now-unused request field is harmless, read the receiving schema, not just the sending code: hauska-engine's dossierRefreshBody is a plain zod z.object (no .strict()), so mcp-server's continued forwarding of the dead verdictLine/brief fields is silently dropped rather than causing a 400. Had that schema been .strict(), leaving those fields in place after this fix would have broken every call instead of merely being cosmetically stale.

The metering side effect (openRisk in CP2 / leave_behind item 2 here) is a genuine, not-yet-ruled product/billing question this lane surfaced but did not resolve: should a genuinely-hollow dossier refresh consume a paid SDK meter now that reaching that determination requires an actual engine call? Whoever merges/deploys PR #83 should either get an explicit ruling first or accept the new behavior knowingly.
